items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: We went into the Paramount Theater, my first time in the Paramount Theater, with Dorothy Lamour and Mischa Auer, and that was our first of quite a few Paramount engagements.

ctx.x: Well, actually there were -- well, we had a wonderful piano player by the name of Nat Jaffe, who was -- he was like Tatum, you know. He wasn't the greatest band piano player in the world, but he had a technique like Art's. I mean he was just fantastic. And the rest of the guys in the band were -- there weren't really any stars. Bobby Burnett was in that band, a trumpet player who was with me for quite awhile after that, there, and later. And we really didn't have -- it was more or less of a team effort, rather…

singular person by the name of Johnny Mendel, not Mandel, but Johnny Mendel, out of Chicago. He was -- that wasn't his real name. He was Polish, and he was one of the sole remaining guys that knew how to growl and use a plunger. And he was in the band. And he played a particularly beautiful solo on a thing that Barney Bigard wrote, called, "Meant For a Lost Love." It's a muted solo with a harmon mute the -- it's one of the prettiest things. I still play it every now and then, when I think of it, because it's so…

trumpet chair and played it unbelievably well. Which of course he wasn't a first trumpet player, but he knew all the charts because he'd written them. And what he couldn't do he'd say, "You play that," you know, and that's when Billy became actually a playing arranger with my band. But in fact that's when we went to four trumpets, because we'd only had three up to that point with that band. And, oh, a couple of years later Glenn Miller stole Billy from me, but he did it by accident. Actually this is very funny.…
